content.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "Today there is a growing awareness that mental well-being needs to be given as much attention as physical health." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.

modelEssay.title: Mental well-being and physical health
modelEssay.content:
Today there is a growing awareness that mental well-being needs to be given as much attention as physical health. This notion arises from the understanding that a sound mind is as crucial as a healthy body.

In the past, physical health was often prioritized over mental health due to the visible nature of physical ailments. However, recent studies have shown that mental health issues can have a profound impact on one's overall well-being, affecting not only personal happiness but also productivity and social interactions. For instance, individuals suffering from depression or anxiety may experience a decline in both their work performance and social life.

In conclusion, it is imperative to recognize the importance of mental health and to invest in resources that promote psychological well-being. By doing so, we can foster a more balanced and healthy society where individuals can thrive both physically and mentally.

transcript.text: Hi Lily, how's the new apartment?

transcript.text: It's OK.

transcript.text: What?

transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 上一周你还对这个地方激动不已，不停地在网上发照片，现在怎么只是还行呢？

transcript.text: Well, last week when I moved in, the apartment seemed cosy, just the right size for one person.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗯，上周我搬进来时，公寓看起来很温馨，一个人住正合适。

transcript.text: But now it just seems tiny, shabby and solitary.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但现在它看起来又小又破旧，还很孤独。

transcript.text: Ah, that's the problem.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 啊，问题就在这里。

transcript.text: You miss your roommates from university, don't you?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你想念大学的室友们，对吧？

transcript.text: I'm going to sound like an idiot because I used to complain to you all the time about how crowded our dormitory room was and about all the things they did to irritate me, like watching movies late at night without headphones or talking loudly early in the morning, but now I miss them terribly.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我听起来会像个傻瓜，因为我过去总是向你抱怨宿舍有多挤，抱怨他们做的那些让我烦的事，比如晚上不戴耳机看电影或一大早大声说话，但现在我非常想念他们。

transcript.text: Of course you do.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你当然会想念。

transcript.text: That's perfectly normal.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这完全正常。

transcript.text: When I got my first place, I remember thinking I couldn't wait to live by myself and get away from my juvenile roommates and all their annoying habits.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我记得我第一次有自己的地方时，迫不及待地想独自生活，远离那些幼稚的室友和他们烦人的习惯。

transcript.text: But then I began missing them and feeling lonely and thinking that our dormitory was like paradise, even though there were six of us guys in one small room.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 但后来我开始想念他们，感到孤独，觉得我们的宿舍就像天堂一样，尽管我们六个男生挤在一个小房间里。

transcript.text: I thought it was just me who felt like that.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我还以为只有我一个人会这样感觉。

transcript.text: Look, you lived at home with us, and then you had three roommates, and this is your first time living alone, so it's hard.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你看，你以前和我们住在家里，然后有三个室友，这是你第一次独自生活，所以很难。

transcript.text: But your first apartment is a milestone in your life, and you should celebrate it.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 但你的第一个公寓是你人生中的一个里程碑，你应该庆祝它。

transcript.text: Tell me about the apartment.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 跟我说说那个公寓。

transcript.text: Actually, it's not bad.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 其实还不错。

transcript.text: In fact, it's pretty adorable now that I have decorated it and it has everything I need.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 事实上，现在它挺可爱的，因为我已经装饰过，而且它有我需要的一切。

transcript.text: I have a kitchen to cook in and a bathroom all to myself, and then another room with my bed at one end and a sofa, a small table, and chairs at the other end.
transcript.speaker: F

transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: Conversation 2.
transcript.translation: 对话二。

transcript.text: Welcome to our program, Book Talk.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 欢迎收听我们的节目，《读书谈》。

transcript.text: Our guest today is Frank Jones, a critic of our education system and the author of a new book, How to Reform Our Universities.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 今天我们请到的嘉宾是弗兰克·琼斯，他是我们教育体系的批评者，也是一本新书《如何改革我们的大学》的作者。

transcript.text: Hello, Susan.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你好，苏珊。

transcript.text: Frank, you support radically changing universities in America.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 弗兰克，你支持对美国大学进行彻底改革。

transcript.text: Yes.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 是的。

transcript.text: I believe that the purpose of higher education is to prepare young people to enter the workforce, and that our current system fails to do this.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我认为高等教育的目的是让年轻人做好进入劳动力市场的准备，而我们当前的体系未能做到这一点。

transcript.text: We're allocating too many resources to disciplines that don't match the needs of employers.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我们把太多资源分配给了与雇主需求不匹配的学科。

transcript.text: I think your attitude to education is a bit cynical, Frank.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我认为你对教育的态度有点愤世嫉俗，弗兰克。

transcript.text: Surely the purpose of university is to prepare young people to participate fully in civic life, rather than just to find well-paid jobs.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 当然，大学的目的是让年轻人充分参与公民生活，而不仅仅是找到高薪工作。

transcript.text: Susan, many young graduates struggle to find any job, let alone a good one.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 苏珊，许多年轻毕业生连找到工作都困难，更别说找到好工作了。

transcript.text: The job market is grim, particularly for students who study the arts.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 就业市场很严峻，尤其是对于学习艺术的学生来说。

transcript.text: I agree that it isn't easy for young people to find work.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我同意年轻人找工作并不容易。

transcript.text: But you propose closing down all departments that aren't directly related to science and technology.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但你提议关闭所有与科学和技术没有直接关系的院系。

transcript.text: Is that really the solution?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 这真的是解决办法吗？

transcript.text: You're overstating my point.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你夸大了我的观点。

transcript.text: My argument is that we need to use more of our budget on areas like science and engineering.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我的论点是，我们需要将更多预算用于科学和工程等领域。

transcript.text: To do that, we need to take money from subjects like literature and music.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 为此，我们需要从文学和音乐等科目中抽出资金。

transcript.text: But the arts have value.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但艺术有价值。

transcript.text: They're an important part of our culture.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 它们是我们文化的重要组成部分。

transcript.text: Studying literature or music or sculpture might not result in a job in that area, but it helps young people to think about the world in a deeper way, which makes them better citizens and makes for a better society.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 学习文学、音乐或雕塑可能不会导致在该领域就业，但它帮助年轻人以更深入的方式思考世界，使他们成为更好的公民，并有助于构建更好的社会。

transcript.text: I agree that the arts are valuable to society.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我同意艺术对社会有价值。

transcript.text: But it's naive to think that not only the most talented, but all students should study them at university level.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 但认为不仅最有才华的学生，而且所有学生都应该在大学阶段学习艺术，这是天真的。

transcript.text: The arts are very competitive and most graduates will end up with a great deal of debt, obtaining a degree that has little value on the job market.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 艺术领域竞争激烈，大多数毕业生最终会背负大量债务，获得的学位在就业市场上几乎没有价值。

transcript.text: Passage one.
transcript.translation: 篇章一。

transcript.text: Do you ever have the annoying feeling that you don't have time to really think anymore?
transcript.translation: 你是否有过这种烦人的感觉，觉得自己再也没有时间真正思考了？

transcript.text: You're not alone.
transcript.translation: 你并不孤单。

transcript.text: A variety of factors have conspired to rob us of time for reflection about ourselves and our lives.
transcript.translation: 多种因素共同作用，剥夺了我们反思自身和生活的时间。

transcript.text: Today, our preoccupied minds are rarely silent.
transcript.translation: 如今，我们心事重重的大脑很少有安静的时候。

transcript.text: The average person receives hundreds of texts and voice messages a day.
transcript.translation: 普通人一天会收到数百条短信和语音消息。

transcript.text: And holidays, for many of us, are action-packed weeks more likely full of family activities than opportunities for tranquility and contemplation.
transcript.translation: 而对于我们许多人来说，假期是活动密集的一周，更可能充满家庭活动，而非宁静与沉思的机会。

transcript.text: Regular reflection, however, underlies all great professionals.
transcript.translation: 然而，定期反思是所有伟大专业人士的基础。

transcript.text: It's a prerequisite for you to recharge your mental batteries, see things in a new light, and tap into your creativity.
transcript.translation: 这是你为精神充电、以新视角看待事物和发挥创造力的先决条件。

transcript.text: Almost all of the great advisors that I have studied have found ways to get away from it all and contemplate their life and work.
transcript.translation: 我所研究的几乎所有伟大顾问都找到了远离尘嚣、思考生活和工作的方法。

transcript.text: Some researchers in the field of creativity, in fact, believe that insight occurs during the reflection and relaxation that follows a period of intense activity.
transcript.translation: 事实上，创造力领域的一些研究者认为，顿悟发生在激烈活动后的反思和放松期间。

transcript.text: Schedule time for reflection about your work or a particular project you're engaged in.
transcript.translation: 安排时间反思你的工作或你正在参与的特定项目。

transcript.text: I usually block out half an hour.
transcript.translation: 我通常预留半小时。

transcript.text: Don't answer the phone.
transcript.translation: 不要接电话。

transcript.text: Push your papers to the side.
transcript.translation: 把文件推到一边。

transcript.text: Sketch.
transcript.translation: 画草图。

transcript.text: Make lists.
transcript.translation: 列清单。

transcript.text: Draw mind maps of ideas that come to you.
transcript.translation: 绘制你脑海中浮现的想法思维导图。

transcript.text: At the end, write down any emerging ideas.
transcript.translation: 最后，写下任何浮现的想法。

transcript.text: When you're alone, stop worrying and think.
transcript.translation: 当你独处时，停止担忧并思考。

transcript.text: A lot of our downtime is spent worrying about troublesome things in our lives or fantasizing about how we'd like our lives to be.
transcript.translation: 我们的很多闲暇时间都花在了担忧生活中的麻烦事或幻想理想生活上。

transcript.text: Revisit things during moments of relaxation after a period of intense work.
transcript.translation: 在高强度工作后的放松时刻重新审视事物。

transcript.text: This is when we are the most creative.
transcript.translation: 这是我们最具创造力的时候。

transcript.text: Passage 2.
transcript.translation: 段落2。

transcript.text: Even before Colorado was a state, it had post offices.
transcript.translation: 在科罗拉多成为州之前，它就已经有了邮局。

transcript.text: The first opened in 1859 in a settlement founded by migrants searching for gold.
transcript.translation: 第一家邮局于1859年在一个由寻找黄金的移民建立的定居点开业。

transcript.text: Life could be unpredictable out west.
transcript.translation: 西部的生活可能难以预测。

transcript.text: Gold failed to appear.
transcript.translation: 黄金没有出现。

transcript.text: Drought ruined farmers and settlers clashed with Native Americans.
transcript.translation: 干旱毁了农民，定居者与美洲原住民发生冲突。

transcript.text: On the settlement's location now stands a sprawling university campus.
transcript.translation: 在定居点的位置上，现在矗立着一个庞大的大学校园。

transcript.text: Amid all the changes, one feature remained constant, the postal service.
transcript.translation: 在所有变化中，一个特点保持不变，那就是邮政服务。

transcript.text: The maps tracing America's westward expansion are telling.
transcript.translation: 追踪美国西进运动的地图很有说服力。

transcript.text: In 1864, there were few postal branches on land controlled by Native Americans, which still accounted for most of the West.
transcript.translation: 1864年，在美洲原住民控制的土地上邮局很少，而这些土地仍占西部的大部分。

transcript.text: Over the next 25 years, post offices grew quickly.
transcript.translation: 在接下来的25年里，邮局迅速增长。

transcript.text: Colonization of the West could be regarded as a result of big government rather than pioneers.
transcript.translation: 西部的殖民化可以被视为大政府的结果，而非开拓者。

transcript.text: As federal subsidies and land grants tempted people into the deserts and plains, the post kept them connected.
transcript.translation: 随着联邦补贴和土地赠与将人们吸引到沙漠和平原，邮政保持了他们的联系。

transcript.text: In the mid 19th century, the post office department was far from a centralized bureaucracy.

transcript.text: To keep up with migration patterns, postal services were added to existing businesses.

transcript.text: The federal government commissioned private wagons to carry the mail.

transcript.text: Short term contracts were granted to local businessmen to act as postmasters.

transcript.text: These partnerships enabled the mail to quickly follow migrants, helping knit together remote parts of the country.

transcript.text: In last week's lecture, we discussed reasons why people forget things.
transcript.translation: 在上周的讲座中，我们讨论了人们忘记事情的原因。

transcript.text: This week, we will discuss a surprising reason why we might remember some things.
transcript.translation: 本周，我们将讨论一个令人惊讶的原因，解释为什么我们可能会记住某些事情。

transcript.text: Anxiety.
transcript.translation: 焦虑。

transcript.text: Think about something as simple as buying a coffee.
transcript.translation: 想想像买咖啡这样简单的事情。

transcript.text: That may not seem like an experience that would make a deep impression on your memory, but anxiety could change that.
transcript.translation: 这可能看起来不会对你的记忆产生深刻印象，但焦虑可能会改变这一点。

transcript.text: In fact, a new study suggests that people with higher anxiety levels might remember certain information better than people with lower anxiety levels.
transcript.translation: 事实上，一项新研究表明，焦虑水平较高的人可能比焦虑水平较低的人更好地记住某些信息。

transcript.text: That's because higher levels of anxiety may make people more susceptible to negative feelings, putting them in a more negative state of mind.
transcript.translation: 这是因为更高的焦虑水平可能使人们更容易受到负面情绪的影响，使他们处于更消极的心态中。

transcript.text: That, in turn, may make them able to better remember some events.
transcript.translation: 这反过来又可能使他们能够更好地记住一些事件。

transcript.text: Let's take a closer look at that new study now.
transcript.translation: 现在让我们更仔细地看看那项新研究。

transcript.text: In the study, the researchers started by giving 80 undergraduate students an anxiety test.
transcript.translation: 在这项研究中，研究人员首先给80名本科生进行了一项焦虑测试。

transcript.text: The test measured the participants' anxiety levels over the preceding two weeks.
transcript.translation: 该测试测量了参与者在过去两周内的焦虑水平。

transcript.text: Then, to test memory, the participants were shown a series of neutral words, one at a time.
transcript.translation: 然后，为了测试记忆，参与者被展示了一系列中性词，一次一个。

transcript.text: Some of the words were printed onto photos of negative scenes, meaning images that could affect their emotions negatively, such as a photo of a car accident or a cemetery.
transcript.translation: 其中一些词被印在负面场景的照片上，即可能对其情绪产生负面影响的图像，如车祸或墓地的照片。

transcript.text: The rest of the words were printed onto photos of neutral scenes, such as a photo of a lake or trees.
transcript.translation: 其余的词被印在中性场景的照片上，如湖泊或树木的照片。

transcript.text: Neutral words included words like table or desk that don't elicit emotion.
transcript.translation: 中性词包括像“桌子”或“书桌”这样不会引发情绪的词。

transcript.text: Later, the participants were asked to think back to the words they were shown earlier, which caused them to re-enter either a negative or neutral mindset.
transcript.translation: 后来，参与者被要求回想他们之前看到的词，这使他们重新进入负面或中性的心态。

transcript.text: The participants were then presented with another set of neutral words, and their memory of these new words was tested.
transcript.translation: 然后，参与者被展示了另一组中性词，并测试了他们对这些新词的记忆。

transcript.text: The researchers found that the new words presented to people in a negative mindset were better remembered by people with higher levels of anxiety than those with lower levels of anxiety.
transcript.translation: 研究人员发现，处于负面心态中的人看到的新词，被焦虑水平较高的人比焦虑水平较低的人更好地记住。

transcript.text: In other words, when highly anxious individuals took in otherwise emotionally neutral information that was presented to them, it became colored by their negative mindset, making them remember the information better.
transcript.translation: 换句话说，当高度焦虑的个体吸收了原本情感中性的信息时，这些信息被他们的负面心态所影响，使他们更好地记住信息。

transcript.text: But these same effects were not seen in people with low levels of anxiety.
transcript.translation: 但这些同样的效果在低焦虑水平的人身上没有观察到。

transcript.text: Previous studies have found that extreme levels of anxiety, such as those experienced by people diagnosed with an anxiety disorder, can be quite detrimental to memory and cognitive performance.
transcript.translation: 先前的研究发现，极端焦虑水平，如被诊断为焦虑障碍的人所经历的，可能对记忆和认知表现相当有害。

transcript.text: But the highly anxious people in this study represent individuals who are managing their anxiety, and for whom anxiety is not a serious problem.
transcript.translation: 但这项研究中的高度焦虑人群代表那些正在管理自己焦虑的个体，对他们来说，焦虑并不是一个严重问题。

transcript.text: Over the past 20 years, the Internet has gradually become a dominant feature of our lives.
transcript.translation: 过去20年来，互联网已逐渐成为我们生活的一个主导特征。

transcript.text: It has changed how we communicate with each other, and it has definitely transformed the way we do business with each other.
transcript.translation: 它改变了我们彼此沟通的方式，并且无疑也转变了我们相互开展业务的方式。

transcript.text: Marketing has also changed in a number of ways.
transcript.translation: 营销也在许多方面发生了变化。

transcript.text: For instance, in the past, consumers had to call a phone number and patiently wait on hold in order to get the information they wanted.
transcript.translation: 例如，在过去，消费者不得不拨打一个电话号码并耐心等待接通，才能获得他们想要的信息。

transcript.text: Today, they want the information immediately.
transcript.translation: 如今，他们希望立即获得信息。

transcript.text: They'll go to the company's social media page and post comments and questions, expecting to receive an immediate response.
transcript.translation: 他们会访问公司的社交媒体页面，发布评论和问题，并期望立即得到回应。

transcript.text: If they don't get their questions answered soon, they'll move on to another company that will answer them quickly.
transcript.translation: 如果他们的问题没有很快得到解答，他们会转向另一家能快速回答问题的公司。

transcript.text: Marketing departments today need to follow technological development.
transcript.translation: 如今的营销部门需要跟上技术发展。

transcript.text: For example, this year's smartphone is smarter than last year's.
transcript.translation: 例如，今年的智能手机比去年的更智能。

transcript.text: Self-driving cars are now on the road.
transcript.translation: 自动驾驶汽车现已上路行驶。

transcript.text: Marketers have to do research on which technologies are coming into being.
transcript.translation: 营销人员必须研究哪些技术正在涌现。

transcript.text: Otherwise, they risk being left behind in the virtual dust.
transcript.translation: 否则，他们就有被远远抛在后面的风险。

transcript.text: Marketing has also changed due to the importance of video.
transcript.translation: 营销的变化还源于视频的重要性。

transcript.text: People don't just want to read text, they want to watch things happening.
transcript.translation: 人们不仅想阅读文字，他们还希望看到事情的发生。

transcript.text: Companies now have to explore how they can use video on a consistent basis to share information about their businesses.
transcript.translation: 公司现在必须探索如何持续地利用视频来分享关于其业务的信息。

transcript.text: Fortunately, it's extremely easy to shoot something these days.
transcript.translation: 幸运的是，如今拍摄内容极其容易。

transcript.text: All you need is a smartphone.
transcript.translation: 你只需要一部智能手机。

transcript.text: But what's the result of all this?
transcript.translation: 但这一切的结果是什么？

transcript.text: Shorter attention spans.
transcript.translation: 更短的注意力持续时间。

transcript.text: We aren't the same people that we were 20 years ago.
transcript.translation: 我们已不再是20年前的我们了。

transcript.text: Not only have we grown accustomed to getting the information we want instantaneously, our attention spans are much shorter.
transcript.translation: 我们不仅已习惯于即时获取我们想要的信息，我们的注意力持续时间也大大缩短了。

transcript.text: If something doesn't capture our attention within a few seconds, we're on to the next piece of content.
transcript.translation: 如果某事在几秒钟内无法抓住我们的注意力，我们就会转向下一条内容。

transcript.text: Marketers need to figure out ways to speak directly to the customer's emotions, and they need to figure out how to do that as quickly as possible.
transcript.translation: 营销人员需要找到直接触动客户情感的方法，并且需要尽快找到实现这一目标的方式。

transcript.text: Once people are emotionally engaged, they'll stick with you.
transcript.translation: 一旦人们在情感上被吸引，他们就会与你保持联系。

transcript.text: If marketing has changed this much in the past 20 years, imagine what the next 20 years will bring.
transcript.translation: 如果说营销在过去20年变化如此之大，想象一下未来20年将会带来什么。

transcript.text: In a recent survey, only 9% of marketers could say with confidence that their marketing efforts were actually working.
transcript.translation: 在最近的一项调查中，只有9%的营销人员能自信地表示他们的营销努力确实奏效。

transcript.text: Their confidence is being shaken because the rules of the game change every year.
transcript.translation: 他们的信心正在被动摇，因为游戏规则每年都发生变化。

transcript.text: That's why it's important for marketers to pay attention to the latest technological developments and consider collaborating with technological innovators.
transcript.translation: 这就是为什么营销人员关注最新技术发展并考虑与技术创新者合作很重要。

transcript.text: That way, they'll be moving at the same pace as the tech industry.
transcript.translation: 那样，他们将能与科技行业同步前进。

transcript.text: You might be surprised to learn that the benefits of friendships extend beyond people's social life and into their work, which is interesting when considering the extent to which people sacrifice friendships or at least the time they spend with friends because of the extended hours they're devoting to work.
transcript.translation: 你可能会惊讶地发现，友谊的好处不仅延伸到人们的社交生活，还延伸到工作中；考虑到人们为了投入更多时间工作而牺牲友谊或至少减少与朋友相处的时间，这很有趣。

transcript.text: Just last week, I was remarking to a colleague that I'm content with only one social engagement per week, but according to recent research, that's evidently not enough.
transcript.translation: 就在上周，我还对同事说，我每周只满足于一次社交活动，但根据最近的研究，这显然还不够。

transcript.text: In an initial study of more than 700 respondents, scholars from an American university analyzed the impact that friends, as opposed to family, have on self-esteem and well-being.
transcript.translation: 在一项针对700多名受访者的初步研究中，一所美国大学的学者分析了朋友（相对于家人）对自尊和幸福感的影响。

transcript.text: Friends came out substantially on top.
transcript.translation: 朋友明显占上风。

transcript.text: That's because to be someone's mate is a voluntary act, unlike family, who people rarely get to choose.
transcript.translation: 这是因为成为某人的朋友是自愿行为，而家人通常不是人们能选择的。

transcript.text: The researchers found that when people choose to cultivate and maintain supportive friendships with an individual, it means that the person is valued and worthy of their limited time.
transcript.translation: 研究人员发现，当人们选择培养和维持与一个人的支持性友谊时，这意味着这个人受到重视，并值得他们投入有限的时间。

transcript.text: Such sentiments of value and worthiness boost our self-esteem.
transcript.translation: 这种价值和 worthiness 的感觉提升了我们的自尊。

transcript.text: The second study comprised more than 300 participants.
transcript.translation: 第二项研究包含300多名参与者。

transcript.text: It proved that the better we feel about ourselves, the more likely we'll perform our job confidently and competently.
transcript.translation: 它证明我们对自己感觉越好，就越有可能自信和胜任地工作。

transcript.text: This follow-up study found that non-work friends even improve people's job satisfaction.
transcript.translation: 这项后续研究发现，非工作朋友甚至能提高人们的工作满意度。

transcript.text: They have as much of an impact on how much they love their jobs as do the friends they have at work, despite not actually being at our place of work.
transcript.translation: 他们对工作的喜爱程度的影响与工作中的朋友一样大，尽管他们实际上不在我们的工作场所。

transcript.text: These types of friends tend to be our preferred outlet for venting about work-related matters.
transcript.translation: 这类朋友往往是我们发泄工作相关事宜的首选渠道。

transcript.text: This is an avenue that may not be available at the office.
transcript.translation: 这可能是办公室中不可用的途径。

transcript.text: So even though friendships can be easy to neglect when confronted by pressures at work, or even pressures at home, neglecting our friends can turn out to be harmful and counterproductive.
transcript.translation: 因此，尽管在面临工作压力甚至家庭压力时，友谊很容易被忽视，但忽视朋友可能是有害且适得其反的。

transcript.text: That's why, when determining how to create a better work-life balance, we need to consider not only how to balance work and family demands, but also how to cultivate and sustain supportive friendships.
transcript.translation: 这就是为什么在决定如何创造更好的工作与生活平衡时，我们不仅需要考虑如何平衡工作和家庭需求，还需要考虑如何培养和维持支持性友谊。

transcript.text: It's for this reason that managers should never discriminate when it comes to requests from employees for flexible work arrangements.
transcript.translation: 正是由于这个原因，管理者在处理员工对灵活工作安排的请求时，绝不应歧视。

The researchers found that dogs are among the more intelligent carnivores (食肉动物), social hunters and domestic animals, but that their intelligence does not __26__ other intelligent animals in any of those categories. Though a significant body of research has examined dog cognition __27__, the authors of this new study found little to warrant the __28__ of work that has been devoted to the topic.

paragraphs.text: Stephen Lea, lead author of the new study, argues that many researchers seem to have designed their studies to __29__ how clever dogs are, rather than simply to study dogs' brains. questionGroups.title: The lifesaving power of gratitude

paragraphs.text: Gratitude may be more beneficial than we commonly suppose. One recent study asked participants to write a note of thanks to someone and then estimate how surprised and happy the recipient would feel—an impact that they consistently underestimated. Another study assessed the health benefits of writing thank-you notes. The researchers found that writing as few as three weekly thank-you notes over the course of three weeks improved life satisfaction, increased happy feelings and reduced symptoms of depression.
paragraphs.translation: 感恩可能比我们通常认为的更有益。一项近期研究要求参与者写一封感谢信给某人，然后估计收信人会感到多惊讶和多开心——他们一直低估了这种影响。另一项研究评估了写感谢信的健康益处。研究人员发现，在三周内每周写三封感谢信就能提高生活满意度，增加幸福感，并减少抑郁症状。

paragraphs.text: While this research into gratitude is relatively new, the principles involved are anything but. Students of mine in a political philosophy course at Indiana University are reading Daniel Defoe's 300-year-old Robinson Crusoe, often regarded as the first novel published in English. Left alone on an unknown island with no apparent prospect of rescue or escape, Crusoe has much to lament (悲). But instead of giving in to despair, he makes a list of things for which he is grateful, including the fact that he is the sole survivor from the shipwreck (海难) and has been able to salvage many useful items from the wreckage.
paragraphs.translation: 虽然这项关于感恩的研究相对较新，但其中涉及的原则绝非如此。我在印第安纳大学政治哲学课上的学生们正在阅读丹尼尔·笛福300年前的《鲁滨逊漂流记》，这通常被认为是第一部用英语出版的小说。独自一人被困在一座未知岛屿上，没有明显的获救或逃脱前景，鲁滨逊有许多值得悲叹的事情。但他没有屈服于绝望，而是列出了一份他感恩的事物清单，包括他是海难中唯一的幸存者，并且能够从残骸中打捞出许多有用的物品。

paragraphs.text: Defoe's masterpiece, which is often ranked as one of the world's greatest novels, provides a portrait of gratitude in action that is as timely and relevant today as it has ever been. It is also one with which contemporary psychology and medicine are just beginning to catch up. Simply put, for most of us, it is far more helpful to focus on the things in life for which we can express gratitude than those that incline us toward resentment and lamentation.
paragraphs.translation: 笛福的杰作经常被列为世界上最伟大的小说之一，它描绘了感恩在实践中的形象，这个形象在今天依然及时且相关。这也是当代心理学和医学刚刚开始追赶的一个方面。简而言之，对我们大多数人来说，关注生活中我们可以表达感恩的事物，比关注那些让我们倾向于怨恨和哀叹的事物更有帮助。

paragraphs.text: When we focus on the things we regret, such as failed relationships, family disputes, and setbacks in career and finance, we tend to become more regretful. Conversely, when we focus on the things we are grateful for, a greater sense of happiness tends to spread through our lives. And while no one would argue for cultivating a false sense of blessedness, there is mounting evidence that counting our blessings is one of the best habits we can develop to promote mental and physical health.
paragraphs.translation: 当我们专注于我们后悔的事情，如失败的关系、家庭纠纷以及事业和财务上的挫折时，我们往往会变得更加后悔。相反，当我们专注于我们感恩的事物时，更大的幸福感往往会蔓延到我们的生活中。虽然没有人会主张培养一种虚假的幸福感，但越来越多的证据表明，数算我们的祝福是我们可以培养的促进身心健康的最佳习惯之一。

paragraphs.text: Gratitude has long enjoyed a privileged position in many of the world's cultural traditions. For example, some ancient Western philosophers counsel gratitude that is both enduring and complete, and some Eastern thinkers portray it as not merely an attitude but a virtue to be put into practice.
paragraphs.translation: 感恩在世界许多文化传统中一直享有特殊地位。例如，一些古代西方哲学家建议感恩要持久且完整，而一些东方思想家则将其不仅仅描述为一种态度，而是一种需要付诸实践的美德。

paragraphs.text: Recent scientific studies support these ancient teachings. Individuals who regularly engage in gratitude exercises, such as counting their blessings or expressing gratitude to others, exhibit increased satisfaction with relationships and fewer symptoms of physical illness. And the benefits are not only psychological and physical. They may also be moral—those who practice gratitude also view their lives less materialistically and suffer from less envy.
paragraphs.translation: 近期科学研究支持这些古老教诲。定期进行感恩练习的人，如数算自己的祝福或向他人表达感恩，表现出对关系更高的满意度和更少的身体疾病症状。这些益处不仅仅是心理和身体的。它们也可能是道德的——实践感恩的人也更少以物质主义视角看待生活，并且更少遭受嫉妒之苦。

paragraphs.text: There are multiple explanations for such benefits of gratefulness. One is the fact that expressing gratitude encourages others to continue being generous, thus promoting a virtuous cycle of goodness in relationships. Similarly, grateful people may be more likely to reciprocate (回报) with acts of kindness of their own. Broadly speaking, a community in which people feel grateful to one another is likely to be a more pleasant place to live than one characterized by mutual suspicion and resentment. The beneficial effects of gratitude may extend even further. For example, when many people feel good about what someone else has done for them, they experience a sense of being lifted up, with a corresponding enhancement of their regard for humanity. Some are inspired to attempt to become better people themselves, doing more to help bring out the best in others and bringing more goodness into the world around them.
paragraphs.translation: 对于感恩的益处有多种解释。其中之一是，表达感恩鼓励他人继续慷慨，从而在关系中促进良性循环。同样，感恩的人可能更可能以自己的善行来回报。广义上讲，一个人们相互感恩的社区可能比一个以相互猜疑和怨恨为特征的社区更宜居。感恩的有益影响可能进一步延伸。例如，当许多人对别人为他们所做的事情感到良好时，他们体验到一种被提升的感觉，并相应地增强了他们对人性的尊重。一些人受到启发，试图自己成为更好的人，更多地帮助他人发挥最佳状态，并为周围世界带来更多善意。

paragraphs.text: Gratitude also tends to strengthen a sense of connection with others. When people want to do good things that inspire gratitude, the level of dedication in relationships tends to grow and relationships seem to last longer. And when people feel more connected, they are more likely to choose to spend their time with one another and demonstrate their feelings of affection in daily acts.
paragraphs.translation: 感恩也往往加强与他人的联系感。当人们想做能激发感恩的好事时，关系中的奉献水平往往会增加，关系似乎更持久。当人们感到更紧密相连时，他们更可能选择花时间在一起，并在日常行为中表达情感。

paragraphs.text: Of course, acts of kindness can also foster discomfort. For example, if people feel they are not worthy of kindness or suspect that some ulterior (别有用心的) motive lies behind it, the benefits of gratitude will not be realized. Likewise, receiving a kindness can give rise to a sense of indebtedness, leaving beneficiaries feeling that they must now pay back whatever good they have received. Gratitude can flourish only if people are secure enough in themselves and sufficiently trusting to allow it to do so. Another obstacle to gratitude is often called a sense of entitlement. Instead of experiencing a benefaction (善行) as a good turn, people sometimes regard it as a mere payment of what they are owed, for which no one deserves any moral credit.
paragraphs.translation: 当然，善行也可能引起不适。例如，如果人们觉得自己不值得善待，或者怀疑背后有别有用心的动机，那么感恩的益处将无法实现。同样，接受善行可能产生一种负债感，让受益者觉得他们现在必须回报所收到的好处。只有当人们足够自信和信任时，感恩才能蓬勃发展。感恩的另一个障碍通常被称为权利感。有时，人们不是将善行视为一种好意，而是将其视为仅仅偿还所欠之物，为此没有人值得任何道德赞誉。

paragraphs.text: There are a number of practical steps anyone can take to promote a sense of gratitude. One is simply spending time on a regular basis thinking about someone who has made a difference, or perhaps writing a thank-you note or expressing such gratitude in person. Others are found in ancient religious disciplines, such as reflecting on benefactions received from another person or actually praying for the health and happiness of a benefactor. In addition to benefactions received, it is also possible to focus on opportunities to do good oneself, whether those acted on in the past or hoped for in the future. Some people are most grateful not for what others have done for them but for chances they enjoyed to help others. In regularly reflecting on the things in his life he is grateful for, Defoe's Crusoe believes that he becomes a far better person than he would have been had he remained in the society from which he originally set out on his voyage.
paragraphs.translation: 有一些实际的步骤任何人都可以采取来促进感恩感。其中之一是定期花时间思考那些产生影响的人，或者写一封感谢信或亲自表达这种感恩。其他方法可以在古代宗教纪律中找到，如反思从他人那里收到的善行或实际为恩人的健康和幸福祈祷。除了收到的善行，也可以关注自己做好事的机会，无论是过去已经做的还是未来希望做的。有些人最感恩的不是别人为他们做了什么，而是他们享受帮助他人的机会。笛福的鲁滨逊通过定期反思生活中他感恩的事物，相信他成为了一个比如果留在他最初出发航行的社会时更好的人。

paragraphs.text: Reflecting on generosity and gratitude, the great basketball coach John Wooden once offered two counsels to his players and students. First, he said, "It is impossible to have a perfect day unless you have done something for someone who will never be able to repay you." In saying this, Wooden sought to promote purely generous acts, as opposed to those performed with an expectation of reward. Second, he said, "Give thanks for your blessings every day."
paragraphs.translation: 反思慷慨和感恩，伟大的篮球教练约翰·伍登曾向他的球员和学生提供了两条建议。首先，他说：“除非你为某个永远无法回报你的人做了点事，否则不可能有完美的一天。”在说这句话时，伍登旨在促进纯粹的慷慨行为，而不是那些期望回报的行为。其次，他说：“每天为你的祝福表示感谢。”

paragraphs.text: Some faith traditions incorporate such practices into the rhythm of daily life. For example, adherents of some religions offer prayers of thanksgiving every morning before rising and every night before lying down to sleep. Others offer thanks throughout the day, such as before meals. Other less frequent special events, such as births, deaths and marriages, may also be heralded by such prayers.
paragraphs.translation: 一些信仰传统将这种实践融入日常生活节奏中。例如，一些宗教的信徒在每天早晨起床前和晚上睡前进行感恩祈祷。其他人则在一天中不断表达感谢，如在餐前。其他不太频繁的特殊事件，如出生、死亡和婚姻，也可能以这样的祈祷来宣告。

paragraphs.text: When Defoe depicted Robinson Crusoe making thanksgiving a daily part of his island life, he was anticipating findings in social science and medicine that would not appear for hundreds of years. Yet he was also reflecting the wisdom of religious and philosophical traditions that extend back thousands of years. Gratitude is one of the healthiest and most nourishing of all states of mind, and those who adopt it as a habit are enriching not only their own lives but also the lives of those around them.
paragraphs.translation: 当笛福描绘鲁滨逊将感恩作为岛上生活日常的一部分时，他预见了社会科学和医学中数百年后才会出现的研究发现。然而，他也反映了延续数千年的宗教和哲学传统的智慧。感恩是所有心态中最健康、最滋养的一种，那些将其作为习惯的人不仅丰富了自己的生活，也丰富了周围人的生活。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: Technology is never a neutral tool for achieving human ends. Technological innovations reshape people as they use these innovations to control their environment. Artificial intelligence, for example, is altering humanity.
paragraphs.translation: 技术从来不是实现人类目的的中立工具。技术创新在人们用其控制环境的同时重塑着人类。例如，人工智能正在改变人类。

paragraphs.text: While the term AI conjures up anxieties about killer robots or catastrophic levels of unemployment, there are other, deeper implications. As AI increasingly shapes the human experience, how does this change what it means to be human? Central to the problem is a person's capacity to make choices, particularly judgments that have moral implications.
paragraphs.translation: 尽管人工智能一词让人联想到关于杀人机器人或灾难性失业水平的焦虑，但还有其他更深层的含义。随着人工智能日益塑造人类体验，这如何改变了“成为人类”的含义？问题的核心是一个人做出选择的能力，尤其是具有道德影响的判断。

paragraphs.text: Aristotle argued that the capacity for making practical judgments depends on regularly making them—on habit and practice. We see the emergence of machines as substitute judges in a variety of everyday contexts as a potential threat to people learning how to effectively exercise judgment themselves.
paragraphs.translation: 亚里士多德认为，做出实践判断的能力依赖于经常做判断——依赖于习惯和实践。我们看到，机器作为替代判断者出现在各种日常情境中，这可能对人们学会如何有效行使判断力构成潜在威胁。

paragraphs.text: In the workplace, managers routinely make decisions about who to hire or fire and which loan to approve, to name a few. These are areas where algorithmic (算法的) prescription is replacing human judgment, and so people who might have had the chance to develop practical judgment in these areas no longer will.
paragraphs.translation: 在工作场所，管理者通常决定雇用或解雇谁以及批准哪些贷款等。这些领域正在被算法处方取代人类判断，因此原本可能有机会在这些领域发展实践判断的人将不再有机会。

paragraphs.text: Recommendation engines, which are increasingly prevalent intermediaries in people's consumption of culture, may serve to constrain choice and minimize luck. By presenting consumers with algorithmically selected choices of what to watch, read, stream and visit next, companies are replacing human taste with machine taste. In one sense, this is helpful. After all, machines can survey a wider range of choices than any individual is likely to have the time or energy to do on their own.
paragraphs.translation: 推荐引擎作为人们文化消费中日益普遍的中介，可能会限制选择并最小化运气。通过向消费者呈现算法选择的观看、阅读、流媒体和访问内容，公司正在用机器品味取代人类品味。从某种意义上说，这很有帮助。毕竟，机器可以审查比任何个人可能有时间或精力自行完成的更广泛的选择范围。

paragraphs.text: At the same time, though, this selection is optimizing for what people are likely to prefer based on what they've preferred in the past. We think there is some risk that people's options will be constrained by their past in a new and unanticipated way.
paragraphs.translation: 然而，与此同时，这种选择是基于人们过去的偏好来优化他们可能喜欢的内容。我们认为存在一种风险，即人们的选择将以一种新的和未曾预料的方式受到他们过去的限制。

paragraphs.text: As machine learning algorithms improve and as they train on more extensive data sets, larger parts of everyday life are likely to become utterly predictable. The predictions are going to get better and better, and they will ultimately make common experiences more efficient and pleasant.
paragraphs.translation: 随着机器学习算法的改进以及它们在更广泛的数据集上进行训练，日常生活中的更大部分可能变得完全可预测。预测将会变得越来越好，最终使常见体验更加高效和愉快。

paragraphs.text: Algorithms could soon-if they don't already—have a better idea about which show you'd like to watch next and which job candidate you should hire than you do. One day, humans may even find a way for machines to make these decisions without some of the biases that humans typically display.
paragraphs.translation: 算法可能很快——如果还没有的话——比你更清楚你想看哪个节目以及应该雇用哪位求职者。有一天，人类甚至可能找到一种方法，让机器在没有人类通常表现出的某些偏见的情况下做出这些决定。

paragraphs.text: But to the extent that unpredictability is part of how people understand themselves and part of what people like about themselves, humanity is in the process of losing something significant. As they become more and more predictable, the creatures inhabiting the increasingly AI-mediated world will become less and less like us.
paragraphs.translation: 但就不可预测性是人们理解自己的方式以及人们喜欢自己的部分而言，人类正在失去一些重要的东西。随着它们变得越来越可预测，居住在日益人工智能中介的世界中的生物将变得越来越不像我们。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Phonics, which involves sounding out words syllable (音节) by syllable, is the best way to teach children to read. But in many classrooms, this can be a dirty word. So much so that some teachers have had to sneak phonics teaching materials into the classroom. Most American children are taught to read in a way that study after study has found to be wrong.
paragraphs.translation: 自然拼读法，即逐音节地拼读单词，是教授儿童阅读的最佳方式。但在许多课堂上，这可能成为一个禁忌词。以至于一些教师不得不偷偷将自然拼读教学材料带入课堂。大多数美国儿童所接受的阅读教学方式，被一项又一项研究发现是错误的。

paragraphs.text: The consequences of this are striking. Less than half of all American adults were proficient readers in 2017. American fourth graders rank 15th on the Progress in International Literacy Study, an international exam.
paragraphs.translation: 其后果令人震惊。2017年，不到一半的美国成年人是熟练的阅读者。美国四年级学生在国际阅读素养进展研究（一项国际考试）中排名第15位。

paragraphs.text: America is stuck in a debate about teaching children to read that has been going on for decades. Some advocate teaching symbol-sound relationships (the sound k can be spelled as c, k, ck, or ch), known as phonics. Others support an immersive approach (using pictures of a cat to learn the word cat), known as "whole language". Most teachers today, almost three out of four according to a survey by the Ed Week Research Centre in 2019, use a mix called "balanced literacy". This combination of methods is ineffective. "You can't sprinkle in a little phonics," says Tenette Smith, executive director of elementary education and reading at Mississippi's education department. "It has to be systematic and explicitly taught."
paragraphs.translation: 美国陷入了一场关于儿童阅读教学的争论，这场争论已经持续了数十年。一些人主张教授符号-声音关系（例如，音素k可以拼写为c、k、ck或ch），即自然拼读法。另一些人支持沉浸式方法（例如，用猫的图片学习单词cat），称为“整体语言法”。如今，根据教育周刊研究中心2019年的一项调查，近四分之三的教师使用一种称为“平衡读写法”的混合方法。这种组合方法是无效的。“你不能只撒一点自然拼读法，”密西西比州教育部基础教育与阅读执行主任特内特·史密斯说。“它必须系统性地、明确地教授。”

paragraphs.text: Mississippi, often behind in social policy, has set an example here. In a state once notorious for its low reading scores, the Mississippi state legislature passed new literacy standards in 2013. Since then Mississippi has seen remarkable gains. Its fourth graders have moved from 49th (out of 50 states) to 29th on the National Assessment of Educational Progress, a nationwide exam. In 2019 it was the only state to improve its scores. For the first time since measurement began, Mississippi's pupils are now average readers, a remarkable achievement in such a poor state.
paragraphs.translation: 密西西比州在社会政策上常常落后，但在这方面树立了榜样。在这个曾经因低阅读分数而臭名昭著的州，密西西比州议会在2013年通过了新的读写标准。自那时起，密西西比州取得了显著进步。其四年级学生在一项全国性考试——国家教育进展评估中的排名从第49位（全50个州）上升到第29位。2019年，它是唯一一个分数提高的州。自测量开始以来，密西西比州的学生现在成为平均水平的阅读者，这在如此贫困的州是一个显著的成就。

paragraphs.text: Mississippi's success is attributed to implementing reading methods supported by a body of research known as the science of reading. In 1997 Congress requested the National Institute of Child Health and Human Development and the Department of Education to convene a National Reading Panel to end the "reading wars" and synthesize the evidence. The panel found that phonics, along with explicit instruction in phonemic (音位的) awareness, fluency and comprehension, worked best.
paragraphs.translation: 密西西比州的成功归功于实施了由一系列研究支持的阅读方法，这些研究被称为阅读科学。1997年，国会要求国家儿童健康与人类发展研究所和教育部召集一个国家阅读小组，以结束“阅读战争”并综合证据。该小组发现，自然拼读法，连同音位意识、流利度和理解力的明确教学，效果最佳。

paragraphs.text: Yet over two decades on, "balanced literacy" is still being taught in classrooms. But advances in statistics and brain imaging have disproved the whole-language method. To the teacher who is a proficient reader, literacy seems like a natural process that requires educated guessing, rather than the deliberate process emphasized by phonics. Teachers can imagine that they learned to read through osmosis (潜移默化) when they were children. Without proper training, they bring this to classrooms.
paragraphs.translation: 然而，二十多年过去了，“平衡读写法”仍在课堂上教授。但统计学和脑成像的进步已经驳斥了整体语言法。对于熟练阅读的教师来说，读写能力似乎是一个需要有根据猜测的自然过程，而不是自然拼读法所强调的刻意过程。教师们可能想象自己小时候通过潜移默化学会了阅读。没有适当的培训，他们将这种观念带入课堂。

questionGroups.sourceText: 近年来，越来越多的中国文化产品走向全球市场，日益受到海外消费者的青睐。随着中国对外文化贸易的快速发展，中国文化产品出口额已持续多年位居世界前列，形成了一批具有国际影响力的文化企业、产品和品牌。数据显示，中国的出版物、影视作品、网络文学与动漫作品等在海外的销售量连年攀升。中国政府出台了一系列政策鼓励和支持更多具有中国元素的优秀文化产品走出国门，扩大海外市场份额，进一步提升中国文化的世界影响力。

answer.modelTranslation: In recent years, an increasing number of Chinese cultural products have made their way to the global market, gaining popularity among overseas consumers. With the rapid development of China's foreign cultural trade, the export value of Chinese cultural products has ranked among the world's highest for many consecutive years, leading to the emergence of a number of cultural enterprises, products and brands with international influence. Statistics show that the overseas sales of China's publications, film and television works, online literature, and animation works have been climbing year after year. The Chinese government has introduced a series of policies to encourage and support more excellent cultural products with Chinese elements to go global, expand their overseas market share, and further enhance the global influence of Chinese culture.
translationNotes: 注意'近年来'的翻译，可用in recent years引导
'越来越多的'译为an increasing number of，也可用more and more
'受到青睐'译为gain popularity among，也可用be favored by
'对外文化贸易'译为foreign cultural trade，也可用cultural trade with foreign countries
'出口额'译为export value；export volume 指出口量，不可混用。'位居世界前列'用rank among the world's highest
'具有国际影响力的'用后置定语with international influence修饰'文化企业、产品和品牌'；不要写成culturally influential，那是'在文化上有影响力'，修饰对象错了
'中国元素'译为Chinese elements，注意固定搭配
'走出国门'译为go global，注意地道表达
'扩大海外市场份额'译为expand their overseas market share，注意使用their指代前文提到的文化产品
'进一步提升'译为further enhance，注意副词的使用
scoringPoints: 准确翻译'近年来'的时间状语
正确使用'越来越多的'的表达(an increasing number of或more and more)
时态使用恰当，主要使用现在完成时表示已经发生并持续的状态
词汇选择准确(foreign cultural trade, export value, with international influence等)
句子结构完整流畅，注意使用连接词(With, leading to, Statistics show that等)
地道表达的使用(go global, expand their overseas market share等)
